answer: The claimant photographs frost on a standard surface at dawn and reports the overnight low, which must sit below the dew point recorded by the nearest public station. A step pale as ivory turns white, a mirror of ice forms on the car roof, and a raven calling from the fence marks the coldest hour. Forging frost for many identities would need many real cold nights in many real places, since a single warm night cannot produce fifty different frosted surfaces.
